scope: Public primary documentation and released issue/release history retrieved read-only for the exact brief. Sources establish external statements, not local product validation.

sources.title: 3MF Core Specification & Reference Guide
sources.version_or_commit: Published Core Specification v1.4.0; change history dated 2025-02-06. The page's exact Git commit was not surfaced.
sources.locator: Sections 1.1 and 2.1 (OPC/ZIP package, parts, optional thumbnail and PrintTicket); 3.1-3.4 (coordinate space, unit default, metadata); 4.2 (components); 5.1 (base material names); 6.1-6.2 (thumbnail and core properties).
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of the official 3MFConsortium specification in GitHub; no implementation or file was run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: 3MF is an OPC ZIP package. Model unit defaults to millimeter if omitted, but permitted values include micron, millimeter, centimeter, inch, foot, meter. Components carry object references and transforms. Base-material names convey portable design intent, while displaycolor is for rendering only; full color/multi-material is extension territory. Package thumbnail and model metadata are optional. PrintTicket is optional and governed by the consumer environment. Required extensions must be supported for processing; recommended extensions call for a consumer warning, and producers should avoid requiring an extension unless key meaning depends on it.
sources.applicability: Format-level normative behavior for 3MF Core 1.4.0; does not guarantee that a specific producer or receiving slicer writes, displays, or preserves every field or extension.

sources.title: Fusion: Save bodies in a component as 3MF, OBJ, or STL files
sources.version_or_commit: Live Fusion help page; no product build/version stated.
sources.locator: Steps 1-9, especially Format, Unit Type, and Structure (lines 20-55 in retrieved page).
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of Autodesk Fusion help; export itself was not performed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Save As Mesh supports 3MF, binary/ASCII STL, and OBJ; explicit unit choices are cm, mm, m, inch, foot. Structure may be one file for all component bodies or one body per file.
sources.applicability: Specific Fusion export workflow; documents UI choices, not the receiving application's interpretation or round-trip fidelity.

sources.title: Fusion: Export designs
sources.version_or_commit: Live Fusion help page; no product build/version stated.
sources.locator: Export format list and tips (especially lines 21-60 in retrieved page).
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of Autodesk Fusion help; no design export performed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fusion lists 3MF and STEP among design export formats. Exported design does not maintain associativity with the original Fusion design. Fusion describes 3MF as a surface-oriented additive format with vertices, triangles, units, colors, textures.
sources.applicability: Specific to Fusion's current help; establishes available routes and a lost-associativity boundary, not a universal description of all STEP encodings.

sources.title: Prusa Knowledge Base: Supported file formats
sources.version_or_commit: PrusaSlicer 2.9 (legacy documentation context); page does not state an exact installed build.
sources.locator: Sections 3MF, STL, STEP, OBJ, and AMF; retrieved article body identifies 3MF as preferred and says STEP is triangulated during import.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of Prusa's official knowledge base; no import performed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: 3MF is the preferred project format; both ASCII and binary STL are accepted; STEP is triangulated during import; OBJ material/texture information is ignored on import.
sources.applicability: PrusaSlicer documented format behavior. Treat its guidance as product-specific and confirm exact receiving release in the pilot.

sources.title: PrusaSlicer issue #8998: STEP import excludes a large part
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2022-10-03 against PrusaSlicer 2.5.0; no confirmed fix/commit was found in the retrieved issue record.
sources.locator: Issue description and reports at lines 155-180; discussion about the OpenCASCADE importer at lines 300-364; subsequent report of same model on 2.5.0.
sources.observed_operation: Read public GitHub issue and comments; attached files were not downloaded and the problem was not reproduced locally.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The report describes STEP geometry with 127 open edges and missing hinge/conical features; the same project worked as STL. Maintainer discussion attributes quality to the importer/OpenCASCADE path. It is issue-history evidence, not proof of behavior in today's release.
sources.applicability: A bounded early-release importer-quality example motivating geometry sentinels when STEP is used; not a blanket rejection of STEP.

sources.title: PrusaSlicer issue #15545: 3MF non-millimetre transform translations
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-07-28; reproducer identifies PrusaSlicer 2.9.6 Windows x64 portable and its SHA-256. Closed by inactivity on 2026-09-29; no fix/PR link appears.
sources.locator: Issue description, reproducible example, expected/actual bounds, control matrix, tested version, and issue activity (lines 151-223, 255-267 in retrieved page).
sources.observed_operation: Read public GitHub issue and reproduction details; package, binary, and generator were not run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For reported Core 3MF inch models, vertices convert to millimeters but build-item/component translation terms do not. Placement can be off by the unit factor and slicing can fail. Issue closure was inactivity housekeeping, not a documented repair.
sources.applicability: Specific reported importer behavior for PrusaSlicer 2.9.6; high relevance to unit/assembly transforms, but not independently reproduced here and no claim about later builds.

sources.title: PrusaSlicer issue #15662: Bambu Studio object names not imported
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-09-02 against PrusaSlicer 3.0.0-alpha11; converted to discussion/locked on 2026-09-03.
sources.locator: Issue description and examples contrasting core 3D model and Metadata/model_settings.config; activity dates.
sources.observed_operation: Read public GitHub issue; example package was not downloaded or tested.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reported names were stored in Bambu-specific model_settings.config rather than core object name fields and were not retained by PrusaSlicer import/resave.
sources.applicability: Shows cross-slicer 3MF project metadata is not interchangeable even when the underlying geometry is in 3MF; alpha-only report, not a statement that Core object names are unsupported.

sources.title: 3MF Consortium specification index
sources.version_or_commit: Specification index accessed 2026-10-10; it lists Core 1.4.0 and Materials & Properties 1.2.1 as published versions.
sources.locator: Specification suite table: Core and Materials & Properties rows.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of official 3MF Consortium specification index.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Materials & Properties is a separately versioned extension (1.2.1) for full-color and multi-material definitions; extension-specific functionality requires a consumer that supports it.
sources.applicability: Version inventory only; detailed extension semantics should be checked against that extension's own text when a pilot depends on it.

sources.title: Prusa Knowledge Base: Saving projects as 3MF
sources.version_or_commit: Prusa knowledge base article; no exact application build stated.
sources.locator: Saving projects as 3MF and 3MF file format sections; retrieved page says project contains objects, settings, modifiers, parameters, and can include thumbnail, color, texture.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of Prusa documentation; no project was saved or opened.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A PrusaSlicer project 3MF may contain a full snapshot including settings and modifiers, not only geometry. The article describes expected same-G-code behavior on another computer and says the format is especially useful for a Prusa receiver.
sources.applicability: PrusaSlicer project behavior; the page itself narrows the strong sharing claim to Prusa-compatible recipients and is not a cross-vendor guarantee.
